_subject.why:
USER, across five pairing notes 2026-09-26: 'no drake to select from' (21-21a), 'missing a drake selection. he's the one they're being compared to. how can we see the difference if he isn't represented as a selection option as well' (20-20), 'need more future img options and drake options' (11-11b), 'no drake anywhere' (28-28), 'no drake' (29-29a).
MEASURED: Drake was an entity on only 8 of 26 beats, while holding 129 candidates in the pool. Of the 18 beats that omitted him, 7 refer to him by PRONOUN ('He gets accused of living on features', 'every song he has ever put on the platform') and 5 by IMPLICATION ('one rapper', 'one dot with open air under it', 'the same slice', 'measured against'). A gazetteer matches capitalised roster names and can reach neither.
This is a single-subject documentary. Every chart in it is a comparison against its subject, so the subject is available on every beat by construction — not extracted, declared. entities.py stays honest: it still reports only what the text names, and this is a separate axis.
